The nanny has to stop the show to take you aside and re-snap your outfit over your now-wet diaper. "Someone got stage fright and made wetties!" The announcement makes your face burn.

choices.label: Ask to Pick Your Own Outfit

success.narration: She's delighted by your initiative! "Of course baby can pick!" You choose something that's still babyish but slightly less humiliating - a cute t-shirt and overalls combo. You feel a bit more comfortable during the show and actually enjoy the attention. You win coins for "Best Self-Expression."

failure.narration: You try to pick something less babyish, but the nanny shakes her head. "That's too big for you! Let Nanny pick." She chooses the MOST humiliating outfit on the rack - a frilly pink dress with matching bonnet and Mary Jane shoes. If you're male-presenting, this is especially mortifying. You have to model this ultra-feminine, ultra-babyish outfit while everyone stares and comments. "Look how pretty baby looks!" The gendered humiliation cuts deep.

choices.label: Refuse to Participate in the Show

success.narration: You politely but firmly decline to participate. A senior nanny respects your choice. "Not every baby likes the spotlight. That's okay!" You're allowed to sit out and watch from the sidelines. You actually have fun watching the others and earn coins for being a good audience member. No forced participation!

failure.narration: Your refusal makes the nannies determined to include you. "Every baby participates!" They forcibly dress you in the most ridiculous outfit - a sissy dress with layers of ruffles, a giant bonnet, white tights, and clicking shoes. They add extra accessories - a bib, a pacifier on a clip, mittens so you can't remove anything. You're paraded down the runway against your will while they hold your hands, announcing: "This is what happens to fussy babies who don't want to participate! We dress them up EXTRA special!" The outfit is so over-the-top that everyone laughs. Midway down the runway, the stress catches up with you - you mess your diaper while walking, the bulk growing noticeable under the short dress. The smell follows you. The nannies notice but make you finish the runway anyway. "Oh my! Someone made a stinky in their pretty dress! Let's give them a round of applause anyway!" The combination of forced feminization, public humiliation, and now a messy diaper is utterly crushing. They leave you in the outfit and messy diaper for another 30 minutes while everyone else gets changed, as punishment for refusing initially.

events.scene: A nanny notices your diaper is wet. But instead of changing you, she smiles mischievously. "I want to test how much this diaper can really hold. Let's see if we can make you leak!" She leads you to a special area with a comfortable chair and produces several large bottles of water. "You're going to sit right here and drink until that diaper fails. Let's find its limit!"

success.narration: You drink two full bottles over the next hour while she monitors your diaper. Your already-wet diaper swells noticeably as you continue to wet yourself. It sags heavily between your legs. But it holds! The diaper doesn't leak. She's impressed. "Good quality diaper! And good baby for helping with the test!" She finally changes you into a fresh one and gives you coins for being a good test subject.

failure.narration: You drink three bottles. Your diaper was already wet to begin with. After the second bottle worth of additional wetting, you feel warmth running down your legs. The diaper has leaked! A puddle forms on the chair beneath you. The nanny claps her hands. "There it is! Leak achieved!" She makes you stand up so everyone can see the wet trails down your legs and the puddle on the chair. "This baby's diaper failed!" The public leak is mortifying. She doesn't change you immediately - first she takes measurements and notes. You stand there in your leaking, failed diaper for several minutes while she documents everything.

choices.label: Ask to Stop After One Bottle

success.narration: She agrees to a modified test. You drink one bottle and wet yourself once more. Your diaper is very heavy but hasn't leaked yet. "Fair enough. Good data point!" She changes you and gives you coins for participating. The test was humiliating but not as extreme as it could have been.

failure.narration: She refuses your request. "The test requires full data!" She makes you drink THREE bottles instead of two as punishment for trying to negotiate. By the third bottle, your diaper absolutely fails. It leaks everywhere - down both legs, onto the chair, even soaking through to your pants. The failure is spectacular and thoroughly documented. She makes you waddle around the nursery in your failed, leaking diaper so everyone can see the result of the test. Wetness drips with each step.

choices.label: Refuse to Participate in the Test

success.narration: You refuse firmly. "This seems like unnecessary humiliation, not a real test." The nanny is surprised by your directness. Another nanny overhears and agrees with you. "Actually, that's a fair point. This isn't very scientific." You're excused from the test and simply given a normal change. You even earn coins for standing up for yourself.

failure.narration: Your refusal angers her. "Refusing a simple test? Fine. We'll make it a REAL experiment then." She calls in other nannies. They hold you down in the chair and force you to drink FOUR bottles - holding your nose, pouring it into your mouth, making you swallow every drop. Your stomach is painfully distended. Your already-wet diaper doesn't stand a chance. It fails catastrophically - leaking from every possible point. But they don't stop. They keep forcing you to drink even after your diaper has failed, making you sit in your puddle. The wetness soaks completely through your clothes. When they finally let you go, you're absolutely drenched from the waist down. They make you walk through the entire nursery to get to the changing area, leaving a trail of drips behind you. Every adult baby and nanny sees your completely failed state. The humiliation is total and absolute. When you finally get changed, they put you in a special punishment diaper - extra thick - and announce to everyone: "This is what happens when babies refuse to cooperate with important testing!"

events.scene: During nap time, a special "sleep therapist" has been brought in to help fussy babies relax. You're led to a quiet room with soft lights and a comfortable reclining chair. The therapist has a soothing voice. "Just relax and watch the mobile spin... listen to my voice... you're getting very sleepy... very little... letting go of all your big thoughts..." You feel yourself slipping into a trance.

success.narration: You slip into a deep trance. The therapist gives you gentle suggestions about feeling safe, comfortable, and accepting your role as a baby. When you wake from the trance an hour later, you feel incredibly relaxed and at peace. You don't remember much but you feel... different. Younger. More accepting. The therapist smiles. "Such a good baby. You did wonderfully." You earn coins and feel genuinely refreshed.

failure.narration: You slip into trance, but the therapist's suggestions go deeper than expected. When you wake, you realize you wet yourself during the hypnosis session - completely unconscious of doing it. The therapist notes it clinically. "Excellent. The subconscious bladder release response worked perfectly." You realize they hypnotized you to wet yourself without awareness. The loss of control during the trance is disturbing and humiliating. Worse, they suggest that "from now on, you'll find it easier and easier to relax into your diaper." You're not sure if that suggestion will stick, but you're worried it might.

success.narration: You manage to maintain some awareness during the trance. You hear the suggestions but they don't fully take hold. When the session ends, the therapist seems disappointed. "This one has strong mental resistance." You avoided the deep conditioning but still earned coins for trying the therapy session.

failure.narration: You try to resist but the hypnosis is too powerful. You slip under despite your efforts. The therapist, realizing you tried to resist, gives you extra strong suggestions as punishment. When you wake, you've not only wet yourself but also messed yourself during the trance - completely unconscious of either. The therapist explains clinically: "Your subconscious was fighting the suggestions, so I had to make them stronger. Your body relaxed completely, including all sphincter control." You wake up in a fully loaded diaper with no memory of it happening. The therapist doesn't change you immediately - they want to "observe how you react to waking up in a messy diaper." You have to sit there, aware you're messy, while they take notes. The clinical humiliation is somehow worse than regular humiliation.

success.narration: You refuse to participate in the hypnosis. The therapist respects your boundary. "Not everyone is comfortable with trance work. That's completely valid." You're excused and even praised for knowing your limits. You earn coins for being assertive about consent.

failure.narration: You refuse, but the therapist insists it's "part of the nursery program" and nannies back them up. You're held in the chair while they force the hypnosis on you - making you watch the spinning mobile, using triggers and techniques despite your protests. Eventually your resistance crumbles and you slip under. But because you fought it, they go much deeper and darker with the suggestions. They plant suggestions that you'll wet and mess yourself at certain triggers - words, sounds, situations. When you finally wake from the forced trance, you're confused and disoriented. The therapist tests one of the triggers immediately - they snap their fingers and say a specific phrase. Against your will, you immediately wet yourself. Your body just... does it. No control. The look of satisfaction on their face is chilling. "Perfect conditioning. Subject will respond to triggers unconsciously." You realize they've programmed you to have accidents on command. They test another trigger - this time for messing. You feel your bowels cramping immediately, uncontrollably. Within minutes, you've completely filled your diaper, unable to resist. The programming worked. The therapist makes notes while you sit there in your full diaper, horrified at what's been done to you. "Excellent results. Subject is now fully controllable." You're sent back to the nursery still in your messy diaper, knowing that certain words or sounds will now make you have accidents involuntarily.

events.scene: The nannies have organized a "Diaper Waddle Race"! All participating adult babies are fitted with extra-thick overnight diapers - much bulkier than normal - that force you to waddle when you walk. The race course is set up across the nursery. A nanny explains the rules: "First baby to waddle to the finish line wins! But there's a twist - every baby has to drink a bottle at the halfway point before continuing!"

success.narration: You waddle along at a moderate pace, the thick diaper crinkling loudly with every step. You drink your halfway bottle without issue and continue. You don't win, but you don't come in last either. The race was silly but fun in its own way. You earn participation coins and the thick diaper is actually pretty comfortable.

failure.narration: You're waddling along when the thick diaper and the bottle at the halfway point combine badly. The pressure of the waddle-walk on your full bladder makes you wet yourself halfway through the race. The thick diaper absorbs it, but it's now even heavier and more bulky. Your waddle becomes even more exaggerated. Other racers pass you while you're dealing with your wet diaper. You finish near last, waddling in a heavy, soaked diaper. Everyone can see how much the diaper has swollen.

success.narration: You waddle as fast as you can, the thick diaper making it comical but you're determined. You chug the halfway bottle quickly and push to the finish. You win! The prize is substantial coins and a trophy. The victory is sweet even if you had to waddle in a ridiculously thick diaper to achieve it. Other adult babies clap for you.

failure.narration: You're pushing hard to win, waddling as fast as possible. But the combination of the thick diaper, the exertion, and the bottle you chugged causes disaster. Near the finish line, in sight of victory, you lose control of your bowels. The thick diaper fills with a massive, warm load that makes the back bulge obscenely. Your waddle becomes almost impossible as the weight shifts with each step. You have to finish the race in your obviously messy diaper. You come in last, waddling to the finish line with a visibly full, sagging diaper while everyone watches and wrinkles their noses at the smell. The nanny announces: "And in last place, the baby who made a big mess during the race!"

success.narration: You spot a shortcut through the play area that the nannies didn't specifically forbid. You take it, waddling through a different route. You emerge at the finish line first! There's a debate among the nannies but they ultimately decide it was clever rather than cheating. You win the big prize and gain a reputation as a "tricky baby."

failure.narration: You try to take a shortcut but are immediately caught by a nanny. "CHEATER!" She grabs you and marches you back to the starting line - but doesn't let you restart. Instead, you're disqualified and given a punishment. She produces an even THICKER diaper and changes you into it in front of all the racers. "Cheaters wear the thickest diapers!" This new diaper is absurdly bulky - you can barely walk, let alone waddle properly. Then she makes you complete the entire race course anyway, after everyone else has finished, wearing this ridiculously thick diaper, while everyone watches and laughs. Midway through your punishment waddle, your overstuffed bowels give up - you mess the already-enormous diaper, making it even more unwieldy. You have to complete your punishment waddle in a massively thick, messy diaper while everyone watches and comments on the smell and your exaggerated waddle. It takes you forever to finish. By the end, you're sweating, exhausted, and thoroughly humiliated.

events.scene: It's the middle of the night. Everyone's asleep in their cribs. You notice that your crib lock is slightly loose. You could potentially escape your crib and explore the dark nursery... or even try to find an exit to the next floor. But you hear a nanny doing rounds in the distance. This is risky. Do you dare try to escape?

choices.label: Stay in Your Crib and Sleep

success.narration: You decide it's not worth the risk. You settle back into your crib and fall asleep. In the morning, you're praised for being a "good sleeper" and earn coins. Sometimes the safe choice is the right choice. You're well-rested and ready for a new day.

failure.narration: You try to sleep but your bladder has other ideas. You wet yourself during the night, soaking your diaper completely. By morning, you've leaked slightly onto your crib sheets. The nanny finds you in the damp crib and sighs. "Someone leaked during the night! What a helpless baby!" You're changed and the crib is cleaned, but the humiliation of having leaked in your sleep lingers.

success.narration: You carefully escape your crib and tiptoe through the dark nursery. You discover secret caches of coins, special items, and even find a map to the next floor's entrance. This exploration was worth it! You slip back into your crib before the nanny's next round. In the morning, no one suspects a thing. You've gained valuable intel and resources.

failure.narration: You escape your crib and start exploring, but you didn't account for the nighttime nanny's schedule. She catches you out of your crib, waddling around in just your diaper in the dark. "What do we have here? A baby out of bed?" Her tone is stern. She scoops you up and carries you not back to your crib, but to a special punishment crib - one with a mesh lid that locks from the outside. "Babies who escape get the secure crib." She locks you in this confined space. The claustrophobic feeling combined with being caught causes stress. Over the next few hours locked in this secure crib, you wet yourself from anxiety, then eventually mess yourself too. You're trapped in your full diaper until morning when she finally lets you out. "Maybe now you'll stay in your crib like a good baby."

choices.label: Try to Find the Exit to Next Floor

success.narration: You escape your crib and navigate through the dark nursery with determination. You find doors, hallways, and eventually - the stairway to Floor 2! This is it! You can advance to the next floor! But... you look down at yourself. You're wearing nothing but a diaper. No clothes, no shoes. Is this how you want to start the next floor? Regardless, you've found the exit. You can choose to proceed now or return to the nursery and leave properly later. You've essentially beaten Floor 1's boss challenge - the ability to escape. Massive coin reward for your bravery and stealth!

failure.narration: You escape your crib and search desperately for an exit. You're sure you're close... but then you hear footsteps. Multiple nannies. They've discovered your escape. "CODE YELLOW! WE HAVE A RUNNER!" What follows is a chase through the nursery. You waddle as fast as you can in your thick nighttime diaper, but they're faster. They corner you near the door you were trying to reach - so close! - and grab you. "Very naughty baby! Trying to escape!" You're carried back into the nursery, but this time you're brought to the Head Nanny's office - a place you've never been. She's waiting, arms crossed. "So. We have a little escape artist." What follows is the most intense punishment of Floor 1. You're strapped into a special restraint chair. They change you into a special "security diaper" - incredibly thick with locking plastic pants over it. A onesie is locked on over that. Mittens are locked on your hands. Booties are locked on your feet. A pacifier gag is locked in your mouth. "You're going to spend the next 24 hours in maximum security baby mode." And they mean it. You're kept in full lockdown baby gear for an entire day. You have to wet and mess these ultra-secure diapers multiple times with no changes offered. They feed you bottles on a schedule. You can't use your hands. You can't speak. You can only waddle awkwardly in the ultra-thick padding. By the end of the 24 hours, you're thoroughly broken, exhausted, and reeking. When they finally remove all the locking gear and change you, the Head Nanny gives you one warning: "Try to escape again, and it'll be 48 hours next time." The experience has traumatized you but also taught you exactly where the exit is. Was it worth it?

events.scene: The nannies have organized an unusual game. All the adult babies sit in a circle while a nanny walks around. "We're going to play a guessing game! I'm going to check everyone's diaper and YOU have to guess if it's wet, messy, or clean before I look!" Other adult babies giggle nervously. Some diapers crinkle suspiciously. Your turn is coming up...

choices.label: Guess Honestly Based on Your Status

success.narration: You accurately report your diaper status and the nanny confirms it with a quick check. "Correct! Good baby for knowing your diaper status!" You earn coins for being honest and self-aware. The game continues around the circle.

failure.narration: You think you know your status, but as the nanny checks you, she discovers something you didn't realize - you've leaked slightly, or there's more wetness than you thought. "Oh my! This baby doesn't even know when they're wet! How babyish!" She announces your actual status to the whole circle while you blush.

success.narration: You claim to be dry when you're actually a bit damp, betting she won't check thoroughly. She does a quick external pat and moves on. You got away with it! The white lie helps you save face in front of the group.

failure.narration: You claim you're clean and dry, but the nanny does a thorough check and discovers you're quite wet - possibly even starting to mess. "LIAR! This diaper is soaked! And I think... yes, someone's making a little present right now!" She holds you in place while you helplessly finish messing your diaper in front of the entire circle during the game. The group watches as your face contorts and the back of your diaper bulges. "Let that be a lesson - always tell Nanny the truth!"

choices.label: Refuse to Participate in the Humiliating Game

success.narration: You politely but firmly say you'd rather not play this game. A senior nanny actually agrees with you. "That's fair - not everyone wants to share that information." You're excused from the circle and can do something else. You earn coins for asserting boundaries.

failure.narration: Your refusal is seen as suspicious. "What's wrong? Does someone have something to HIDE?" The nanny insists on checking you extra thoroughly in front of everyone as "punishment for not playing along." She pulls your pants down, pulls your diaper away from your body at multiple angles, even spreads your cheeks slightly to check for messes. The invasive, public inspection is mortifying - and the stress of it makes you start wetting yourself DURING the check. She feels it happening. "Oh! And look - refusing to play made this baby so nervous they're peeing themselves RIGHT NOW during inspection! Everyone watch!" The circle stares as your diaper grows warm and heavy while she's still holding it open.

events.scene: A mischievous nanny gathers a small group of adult babies. "Let's play a little game. I want to see who's REALLY embraced being a baby. The challenge is simple: the first one to have a 'natural accident' without being told to wins a big prize! Just go about your play normally... and let nature take its course." She watches with a knowing smile as you all exchange nervous glances.

choices.label: Play Normally and Let It Happen Naturally

success.narration: You genuinely get absorbed in playing with toys and after about 15 minutes, you wet your diaper without really thinking about it - almost like a real accident. The nanny claps. "We have a winner! This baby is so regressed they didn't even notice!" You win a substantial prize despite the humiliation. The natural regression actually felt... oddly liberating.

failure.narration: You try to let it happen naturally but you're too aware of the game. You hold back self-consciously. Another baby beats you to it, wetting themselves with an obvious expression of relief. You lose the challenge and don't get the prize. Worse, the nanny notices your self-consciousness. "This one's still thinking too much like a big kid. Needs more regression training." She marks you down on her clipboard.

choices.label: Try to Win by Messing First

success.narration: You deliberately relax your bowels and mess your diaper first, beating everyone else. The nanny is impressed. "Oh my! Someone went all the way! This baby REALLY committed to the game!" You win the grand prize - though you now have to sit in your messy diaper while she awards it. The combination of victory and humiliation is complex.

failure.narration: You try to force yourself to mess but your body won't cooperate with the conscious command - nothing happens. Meanwhile, another baby wets themselves naturally and wins. Your obvious straining was noticed by the nanny. "Were you trying to force it? That's not natural! That's cheating!" She disqualifies you from the prize AND makes you do corner time for trying to game the system instead of letting it happen naturally.

success.narration: You maintain perfect control, refusing to play their game. After 30 minutes with no winner, the nanny gives up. "Fine, no prize for anyone then!" But another nanny privately approaches you afterward. "I'm impressed you maintained that much control. Here's a secret reward." You get coins and respect for your willpower.

failure.narration: You try to maintain control to avoid participating, but your body has other plans. After 20 minutes of trying to hold everything while playing, the pressure becomes unbearable. You lose control catastrophically - wetting AND messing your diaper in quick succession, losing the 'game' in the most humiliating way possible. The nanny laughs. "Look at this! Tried to resist but became the BIGGEST baby of all! Lost complete control!" You don't get the prize, but you get maximum humiliation instead. She makes you continue playing in your full diaper for another 15 minutes before changing you.

events.scene: A nanny announces "Pacifier Training Time!" All adult babies are given large pacifiers. "Everyone needs to keep their paci in their mouth for the next hour. If it falls out, you get a demerit. Three demerits and you get a punishment. Now... let's see how you do!" The pacifier is bigger than you expected and makes it hard to swallow normally. Drool is inevitable.

choices.label: Keep the Pacifier In as Instructed

success.narration: You manage to keep the pacifier in your mouth for the full hour, though you drool embarrassingly into a bib. Your jaw aches slightly but you did it. The nanny praises you and gives you coins. "Such a good paci-baby!" The hour of enforced silence was actually somewhat peaceful.

failure.narration: You try to keep it in but the pacifier keeps falling out - when you try to talk, when you yawn, when you shift position. By the end of the hour you have three demerits. Your "punishment" is that you have to wear a pacifier gag instead - one that straps around your head and CAN'T fall out. You have to wear it for the next two hours. The inability to remove it or speak becomes frustrating. Even worse, you eventually need to wet your diaper but can't even ask for permission or a change. You just have to do it and waddle around in it silently until someone notices.

choices.label: Try to Communicate Despite the Pacifier

success.narration: You find creative ways to communicate - pointing, gestures, muffled sounds around the pacifier. The nanny finds it adorable. "Look at baby trying so hard to talk! So cute!" Other adult babies copy your methods. You successfully maintain communication while keeping the pacifier in. You earn coins for creative problem-solving.

failure.narration: Your attempts to talk around the pacifier just make you spray drool everywhere and produce unintelligible baby babbles. The nanny laughs at your efforts. "Aww, listen to the baby talk! Someone's really embracing being little!" She interprets all your attempted communication as baby babble, leading to frustrating misunderstandings. When you try to indicate you need the bathroom, she thinks you want your stuffed animal and gives you that instead. You end up wetting your diaper because you couldn't effectively communicate.

success.narration: You spit it out and state firmly: "I'm not doing this." A senior nanny witnesses your defiance and surprisingly respects it. "This one's showing autonomy. Let them opt out." You're excused from pacifier training entirely and earn significant coins for standing your ground.

failure.narration: You spit it out defiantly multiple times. This earns severe consequences. The nanny produces a locking pacifier gag - a large one with a rubber bulb that fills your mouth. "Since you won't keep your paci in voluntarily, we'll make sure you CAN'T spit it out." She straps it on tightly. The bulb makes your jaw ache and makes swallowing difficult. Drool flows freely. You're kept in this for THREE hours as punishment, unable to speak, barely able to swallow. By the end, you've drooled all over yourself and wet your diaper twice from being unable to ask for any relief. Your jaw is sore, you're frustrated, and thoroughly humiliated. When she finally removes it, your mouth is raw and you can barely talk anyway.

events.scene: A nanny intentionally does something frustrating - maybe gives your favorite toy to another adult baby, or tells you 'no' to something reasonable. She watches you with a knowing expression, clearly waiting to see if you'll throw a tantrum. Other babies around you ARE throwing tantrums - crying, stomping, pouting. It seems almost... expected here?

choices.label: Accept It Calmly Like an Adult

success.narration: You take a deep breath and accept the frustration without tantruming. The nanny looks impressed. "My my, such emotional control! Here, you can have it back for being so mature." She returns what she took and gives you bonus coins for self-control. Sometimes the adult response works.

failure.narration: You try to be calm but your face betrays your frustration. The nanny sees it. "Oh, is baby upset? Are you going to cry about it? Go ahead, let it out!" Her encouragement paradoxically makes it worse. You feel tears welling up despite yourself. She coos as you actually start crying. "There's my real baby!" The loss of emotional control is humiliating, especially when you realize you're genuinely upset over something so childish.

choices.label: Throw a Small Tantrum to Fit In

success.narration: You put on a show - pout, whine a little, stomp your foot. The nanny eats it up. "Aww, baby's fussy! Okay okay, here you go." She gives you what you wanted plus treats for "being such a good little baby about your feelings." The calculated regression paid off, though playing the part felt oddly natural.

failure.narration: You try to throw a 'fake' tantrum but it spirals out of control. The emotional regression becomes real - you're genuinely upset, crying real tears, stamping your feet, maybe even dropping to the floor. You lost control of the performance and now you're having an actual meltdown. The nanny watches with satisfaction as you cry yourself out. When you finally stop, exhausted, you realize you wet your diaper at some point during the tantrum without even noticing. "Feel better now that you got that out, baby?" she asks smugly.

success.narration: You calmly state: "You're deliberately trying to make me tantrum. I'm not playing that game." Your directness surprises her. Another nanny overhears and reprimands her. "We don't manipulate the babies like that!" You're given an apology AND significant coins for calling out inappropriate behavior.

failure.narration: You try to call out the manipulation but it comes out whinier than you intended - almost like... a tantrum itself. "You're being mean on PURPOSE! You WANT me to cry! It's not FAIR!" The nanny grins wickedly. "Aww, listen to baby! Is baby getting fussy? Does baby need a timeout?" She puts you in timeout facing the corner for "arguing with Nanny." But that's not all - she periodically comes by to poke fun at you. "Still pouting in timeout? Such a fussy baby!" The timeout lasts 30 minutes during which you have no way to occupy yourself. Boredom and frustration build. By the end, you're genuinely emotional, and yes - you wet your diaper during timeout because you couldn't ask to leave or be changed.

events.scene: A nanny approaches with a camera and a big smile. "Great news! The diaper company wants to do an advertisement featuring our nursery! You've been selected to be in it!" She holds up an EXTREMELY babyish diaper - thick, crinkly, covered in cartoon characters. "You'll model this special diaper while we film you playing. Everyone will see how well it works!" This will be shown... publicly?

success.narration: You agree and they dress you in the ridiculous diaper. The photo shoot is embarrassing but brief - they take pictures of you playing with toys, sitting, crawling. The diaper is incredibly thick and obvious. But when it's done, they pay you handsomely with coins and even give you a gift basket. The photos will exist somewhere, but at least you got paid.

failure.narration: You agree to model, and at first it's just photos. But then: "Let's get some 'action shots'! Show us how the diaper performs!" They want you to actually WET the diaper on camera. And they won't take no for an answer - you signed up for this. With cameras rolling and crew watching, you're pressured to wet yourself in the ridiculous diaper. The warmth spreading is captured on film. They make you continue 'playing' in the wet diaper while they document how well it absorbs. "Great! Now let's get some shots from the back - stand up and bend over!" They photograph your wet, saggy diaper from every angle. The whole production is mortifying. At least the pay is good... but those photos exist forever now.

success.narration: You negotiate: more money, face blurred in photos, right to approve final images. They agree to your terms! The shoot proceeds but you maintain some control and dignity. The pay is substantial and your identity is protected. This was actually a smart business decision.

failure.narration: You try to negotiate but they're offended. "We specifically CHOSE you and you're making demands? Fine, we'll use someone else!" They pick a different adult baby who's much more enthusiastic. You watch as that baby gets paid triple what you would have earned, gets special treatment, and becomes the "star baby" of the nursery for the rest of the day. You missed out on a huge opportunity because you overthought it.

choices.label: Refuse to Be in the Advertisement

success.narration: You firmly refuse. "I don't consent to being filmed or photographed in diapers." They're disappointed but legally can't force you. A nanny actually respects your boundary. "That's valid. Consent matters." You're excused without penalty and even get coins for knowing your rights.

failure.narration: You refuse, but they insist. "You signed a general photo release when you entered the nursery! We have the right!" Nannies physically hold you while they force the diaper onto you. The group executes the plan successfully - you all sneak out together and discover an alternative exit to Floor 2. You advance without needing nanny approval! The resistance gives you special items and massive coins for being part of the successful escape. You feel like you beat the system!

failure.narration: You attend the meeting but it's a trap! The nannies knew about it all along - one of the "resistance" was a plant. Nannies flood in. "Caught you ALL!" Everyone at the meeting is captured. The punishment is severe: all of you are put through intensive regression therapy for 48 hours. You're kept in maximum restriction gear - thick diapers, locking onesies, mitts, pacifier gags. You're bottle-fed on schedules. You're forced to use your diapers repeatedly with no changes for hours at a time. The therapy is designed to break your adult awareness. By the end, you're exhausted, humiliated, and deeply regressed. The resistance is crushed. Worse, you're denied advancement for an additional 72 hours as punishment. The failed escape attempt set you back significantly.

choices.label: Betray the Resistance to the Head Nanny

success.narration: You immediately report the resistance to the Head Nanny. She's extremely grateful. "You've done the nursery a great service." The resistance is rounded up and you're rewarded handsomely - massive coins, instant approval to advance to Floor 2, a letter of recommendation, and permanent "trusted baby" status. The Head Nanny personally thanks you. You advanced by choosing loyalty to authority over solidarity with fellow trapped babies. The resistance members will hate you forever, but you got what you wanted.

failure.narration: You try to betray the resistance but they anticipated this possibility - they were testing you. Before you can reach a nanny, resistance members intercept you. "We knew you might try this." They drag you to a hidden area. What follows is brutal: they restrain you and force-feed you massive amounts of laxative juice and diuretics. "Let's see how the snitch likes being a helpless baby." They lock you in a storage closet - alone, restrained, unable to call for help. Over the next few hours, your body processes everything. You wet yourself repeatedly, soaking through multiple diapers. You mess yourself massively, multiple times, with no one to change you. By the time they release you hours later, you're in a completely destroyed diaper, covered in your own filth, exhausted and broken. They scatter before anyone finds you. When nannies discover you in the closet in your horrific state, you try to explain what happened but they think you're making up stories. "Sounds like someone got into the supply closet and made a mess of themselves!" The resistance got away with their revenge. You're left humiliated, reeking, and with no advancement. Both sides hate you now - resistance babies know you tried to snitch, and nannies think you're irresponsible. You've made enemies everywhere.

success.narration: You decline respectfully. "I appreciate the offer but I'm not interested in competing." Jordan nods. "Smart. You know your limits." You avoid potential conflict. Jordan actually respects your honesty and gives you some basic advice anyway. Small coins earned.

failure.narration: You decline, but Jordan takes it as cowardice. "Thought so. Too scared to compete." They spread word that you're a weakling. Other babies start treating you as the lowest in the hierarchy. Your refusal to compete cost you social status among the babies.

They give you crucial information: "The Head Nanny has a weakness. If you can make yourself indispensable to her - become her favorite - she'll fast-track your advancement." This intelligence is valuable. You also earn respect from other babies. Jordan becomes your ally rather than rival. You've shifted the power dynamics! Substantial coins earned plus new strategic information.
success.statusEffect: Respected by Alpha Baby - High Status

failure.narration: Jordan beats you at the puzzle challenge. You lost. Now you're Jordan's baby for the rest of Floor 1. Other babies see you as Jordan's property. You're stuck in this dynamic until you can advance floors. The loss cost you dignity and autonomy.

You've won Floor 1 through social dominance!

failure.narration: You challenge Jordan to a race but lose badly. The loss has made your time on Floor 1 miserable. You'll need to advance floors just to escape this nightmare.

events.scene: A mysterious nanny you've never seen before approaches you during a quiet moment. "I'm not like the other nannies. I'm here to evaluate special cases. I've been watching you. I think you might be ready for a... different kind of advancement. One that doesn't require traditional regression. Come with me to a private testing area. If you pass my tests, I can authorize your immediate advancement to Floor 2. But my tests are... unconventional. Are you willing to try?"

success.narration: You politely decline. "Thank you, but I'd prefer to advance through the normal channels." The mysterious nanny nods. "Wise to be cautious. Good luck with your traditional path." You avoided an unknown risk. Sometimes the devil you know is better.

failure.narration: You decline, but the mysterious nanny seems offended. "I don't offer this opportunity often. You've insulted me by refusing." Later, you notice obstacles in your traditional advancement path - your applications get "lost," nannies are less helpful. The mysterious nanny is subtly sabotaging you for rejecting their offer.

You solve riddles, navigate moral dilemmas, and demonstrate strategic thinking - all while wearing just a diaper. You pass! failure.narration: You accept the tests but fail them. The tests were too complex - you couldn't solve the riddles, made poor choices in the moral scenarios, and struggled to think strategically while in regression headspace. You're marked as someone who tried to cheat the system.

choices.label: Accept But Propose Your Own Test

"You've earned the VIP treatment. Good luck on your journey." You've achieved the best possible outcome for Floor 1!

failure.narration: You challenge their authority and demand to test them. They're insulted. "You DARE question ME?" They reveal they actually ARE authorized - they show credentials. For 48 hours you're kept in complete baby mode - pacifier gag locked in, mittens on hands, thick diapers, fed only bottles, no toys, maximum supervision. Every aspect of autonomy is stripped away. success.statusEffect: GAME OVER - Alternative Ending: Chose to Stay

Your self-preservation instinct was valid - maintaining awareness of the danger helps you stay focused on advancement.

Worse, watching Maya casually wet and mess their diaper during play somehow makes you feel like it's okay to do the same. You wet yourself during the forced playtime, almost without thinking about it. Maya's regression was contagious.

Having an adult conversation while wearing diapers is surreal but welcome. Alex shares intelligence about nanny schedules and gives you coins. "Stay sane out there. Don't let them get too deep in your head." You feel more grounded after talking to someone else resisting.

Alex shoots you an apologetic look as you're taken away. The punishment: you both have to wear humiliating bibs that say "I THINK I'M A GROWN-UP" for the rest of the day. The attempt at adult connection backfired.

choices.label: Warn Alex Their Resistance is Dangerous

success.narration: You gently warn Alex: "Fighting too hard will make it worse. Sometimes you have to play along to advance." Alex considers this. "You might be right. Thanks." Your advice helps them adjust their strategy. Later, Alex successfully advances to Floor 2 and leaves you a thank-you gift of coins and a note: "Your advice helped. Good luck. - A"

failure.narration: Alex takes your warning as criticism. "Oh, so you think I should just GIVE IN? Become like Maya, drooling and babbling? Fuck that." They're offended. Your relationship is damaged. You both successfully advance to Floor 2 together, earning massive coins and special items. "Couldn't have done it without you," Alex says as you both move to the next floor.

failure.narration: You suggest partnering up but Alex's resistance attracts too much nanny attention. Your association with them gets you BOTH flagged as "problem babies." I've found that helping others helps me cope with being here."

success.narration: You accept Jordan's offer. They sit with you, play alongside you, and genuinely listen when you talk about the struggles of being here. Their kindness is healing. Jordan even shares some of their snacks with you. "We're all in this together. No reason not to help each other." You feel better after spending time with them. Jordan becomes a friend and support system. They give you coins and ongoing emotional support.

"It's okay, let it out." The emotional release is cathartic but embarrassing. A nanny sees you crying and assumes you're having a regression moment. "Aww, baby's having big feelings! Time for a comfort change and a nap." You're taken away from Jordan for "comfort care" - bottle feeding, thick diaper change, forced nap time. The vulnerability led to unwanted regression treatment.

success.narration: You decline: "I appreciate it but I'm okay. I need to handle this myself." Jordan understands. "Totally fair. Offer stands if you change your mind." Your independence is respected. Jordan doesn't push. You maintain your autonomy while keeping the door open for future interaction. You earn coins for self-reliance.

What follows is Jordan becoming your unofficial caregiver. They check on you regularly, help you with challenges, comfort you when things are hard, even help change your diaper when nannies are busy. Having a caring peer provide this level of support is deeply comforting. You regress more under their care but it feels safe and intentional. Jordan becomes your anchor in the nursery. The relationship helps you cope with everything. You both advance together eventually, having formed a deep bond.
success.statusEffect: Jordan is Your Caregiver - Deep Bond

The relationship becomes strained. You're caught in an unwanted dynamic where Jordan has taken your request too far and now treats you as genuinely helpless. Nannies notice and start treating you the same way. Your request for care accidentally convinced everyone you're more regressed than you are.

I don't belong here!" They're fighting the nannies, refusing to wear the diaper, on the verge of a breakdown. You remember feeling like that. Do you help them adjust or let them figure it out?

success.narration: You approach Taylor calmly. "I know this is overwhelming. I was like you when I arrived. But fighting makes it worse. Let me help you understand how things work here." Taylor is desperate for any help. You guide them through the basics - how to interact with nannies, how to pick battles, survival strategies. Taylor is immensely grateful. "Thank you for not letting me go through this alone." They become a loyal friend. As Taylor adjusts, they share resources with you. Having helped the new arrival makes you feel more competent and grounded.

success.narration: You decide not to interfere. Taylor needs to find their own way just like you did. Over the next few days, Taylor eventually calms down and adjusts. You've gained a friend who appreciates boundaries.

You wonder if intervening earlier might have prevented this. Taylor doesn't really remember you now. Watching their deterioration was disturbing.

You both work toward escaping together.

events.scene: Finley runs an underground economy in the nursery. They trade everything - toys, information, favors, even contraband items. During free time, Finley approaches you with a business proposition. "You look like someone with potential. I could use a partner. Help me run my operation and we split the profits. Interested?"

success.narration: You decline politely: "Thanks, but I'd rather not get involved in black market stuff." Finley nods. "Fair enough. Door's always open if you change your mind." You can still buy from Finley occasionally without being part of the operation. You maintain access to the black market without the risks of running it.

failure.narration: You decline but Finley takes it personally. "You think you're too good for this?" They cut you off from the black market entirely. When you need something later, Finley refuses to trade with you. "Should've partnered up when you had the chance." You've lost access to valuable underground resources.

success.narration: You agree to partner with Finley. The black market operation is lucrative! You help source items, make connections, facilitate trades. The profits are substantial. You're making serious coins. Finley teaches you the underground economy - who wants what, how to price things, how to avoid nanny attention. The partnership thrives. You both accumulate wealth that makes advancement easier. Having Finley as a business partner provides ongoing income and resources throughout your time on Floor 1.

failure.narration: You partner with Finley but the operation gets busted. Nannies discover the black market. "Unauthorized trading! Contraband items!" Both you and Finley are punished. Your inventory is confiscated - you lose all coins and items. You're both put in "economic timeout" - restricted from trading anything for two weeks. During this time you can't buy or sell, can't trade, can't even share snacks. The forced poverty is frustrating. The partnership that was supposed to make you rich got you stripped of everything.

choices.label: Try to Take Over the Operation

success.narration: You accept the partnership but secretly plan to take over. You learn Finley's contacts, trade routes, and secrets. Then you make your move - you undercut Finley's prices, offer better deals, and gradually steal their customer base. Finley realizes too late what's happening. "You... you betrayed me!" But by then you've taken over the black market. You're now the sole merchant. The profits flow entirely to you. Finley is bitter but powerless. "You're ruthless. I respect it... but I'll never forgive it." You've made an enemy but gained a monopoly. The massive coins and power make advancement trivial. You're the richest baby on Floor 1.

failure.narration: You try to take over but Finley was three steps ahead. "You think I didn't see this coming?" Finley had contingencies. They've already warned their contacts about you. When you try to trade, nobody trusts you. "Finley says you're a snake." Your attempted takeover failed and destroyed your reputation. But Finley doesn't stop there - they actively sabotage you. They spread rumors, tank your deals, even frame you for things you didn't do. Nannies investigate you for "suspicious behavior." You're put under scrutiny. Your coins are audited and some are confiscated as "ill-gotten." The failed takeover attempt made a powerful enemy who's now actively destroying you. Finley's network is being used against you. Your reputation is ruined, you've lost coins, and you're under investigation. The power grab was a disaster.

events.scene: Sage sits in the corner during play time, clearly deep in thought despite wearing a thick diaper and holding a teddy bear. When you approach, Sage looks up. "I've been thinking about the philosophy of this place. We're adults being treated as infants. But aren't we already all just helpless beings pretending to have control? Maybe this place is just making explicit what was always true. Want to discuss existentialism while wearing diapers? It's surreal but... interesting."

success.narration: You engage Sage in deep philosophical discussion. Talking about the nature of autonomy, the social construction of adulthood, the arbitrary nature of dignity while literally wearing diapers is absurd but intellectually stimulating. Sage shares profound insights about the experience. "Perhaps regression isn't losing something but gaining permission to be vulnerable." The conversations help you process your experience intellectually. Sage becomes a valued friend who helps you make meaning of this strange situation. You earn coins and philosophical clarity.

failure.narration: You try to engage philosophically but the absurdity overwhelms you. Discussing Foucault's theories of power while sitting in a wet diaper just feels ridiculous. You start laughing at the incongruity and can't stop. Sage is offended. "I was being serious." The laughter was inappropriate. Sage thinks you were mocking them. The philosophical friendship opportunity is lost because you couldn't maintain the intellectual seriousness while in such an undignified physical state.

success.narration: You argue: "But there IS a difference between chosen vulnerability and forced regression. Philosophy can't rationalize away real power dynamics." Sage considers this. "You're right. I was perhaps too abstract. The lived experience of powerlessness is different from theoretical vulnerability." Your critique deepens the discussion. Sage appreciates the pushback. Together you develop a more nuanced philosophy that acknowledges both the arbitrary nature of adult dignity AND the real harm of forced infantilization. The intellectual partnership produces genuine insight. You co-write a philosophical text about the experience that sells well to other intellectually-minded babies.

failure.narration: You challenge Sage's philosophy but it devolves into an argument. "You're being reductive!" "No, YOU'RE being naive!" The intellectual debate becomes heated. Other babies watch uncomfortably as you two argue about Kant and Hegel while wearing diapers. A nanny intervenes. "No fighting! Both of you, timeout!" You're both put in timeout corners for "arguing during play time." The philosophical disagreement got you both punished. Sage blames you for escalating. The intellectual connection is poisoned by the conflict.

success.narration: You suggest: "Maybe we should stop trying to intellectualize this and just... experience it. Let go of the need to make meaning." Sage is shocked at first, then intrigued. "That's... actually profound. The philosophy of anti-philosophy. Embracing the pre-cognitive experience." You both decide to experiment with pure experience - no analysis, no intellectualizing, just being babies without the adult mind commentary. The practice is liberating. By releasing the need to philosophize everything, you both find unexpected peace. The irony is that abandoning philosophy was itself a philosophical move - but you're not analyzing that. You're just experiencing. The practice helps both of you regress more comfortably while maintaining core awareness. You advance together with a zen-like acceptance.

failure.narration: You suggest abandoning philosophy but Sage takes it as an insult to their coping mechanism. "So you think intellectualizing is wrong? It's how I SURVIVE this!" They're deeply hurt. "You're basically telling me to just accept being a mindless baby!" That wasn't what you meant but Sage heard it that way. Your suggestion to abandon meaning-making felt like invalidation of Sage's primary coping strategy. Sage avoids you afterward. Worse, Sage tells other intellectual babies that you're "anti-intellectual" and "gave up." You've alienated the entire philosophical circle in the nursery. The suggestion to abandon philosophy got you labeled as someone who's given up on maintaining adult cognition. The philosophical babies view you with pity or disdain now.

events.scene: You encounter someone who looks exactly like you. Same face, same build, wearing an identical diaper. But something's different - they seem more worn down, or perhaps more at peace? They approach you with a knowing smile. "I'm you. From a different timeline. I already made the choices you're about to make. Want to know how it turns out? Or would you rather not know?"

success.narration: You turn and walk away without speaking to your doppelgänger. Some things are better not knowing. The figure doesn't follow. You make your own choices without being influenced by future knowledge. Your path remains yours alone. You maintain agency over your destiny. You earn coins for trusting your own judgment over potential future knowledge.

failure.narration: You try to walk away but you can't stop glancing back. The temptation to know is overwhelming. You stop. Turn back. "Wait... what can you tell me?" But when you look, the doppelgänger is gone. The opportunity to learn from your other self is lost. You're left with just the unsettling knowledge that alternate versions of you exist somewhere in this game. The encounter planted seeds of doubt without providing any answers.

success.narration: You ask your alternate self: "What should I do? What happens on the next floors?" They share crucial information about Floors 2-5, warning you about specific dangers and opportunities. "On Floor 3, don't trust the one who offers you a shortcut. On Floor 5, do exactly what they tell you even if it seems wrong." The intelligence is invaluable. Your alternate self gives you items and coins they've collected. "I already climbed this high. Now you can benefit from my experience." The meeting was beneficial - you're essentially getting a walkthrough from your future self. Armed with this knowledge, your chances of success increase dramatically.

failure.narration: You ask questions but the answers disturb you. "You don't make it past Floor 7. You break there. It's too much." Your alternate self looks haunted. "I came back to warn you. Maybe if you know ahead of time, you can prepare better than I did. But honestly? I don't think anyone can prepare for Floor 7." The knowledge of your eventual failure is crushing. Your alternate self sees your despair. "I've made it worse, haven't I? I thought warning you would help but now you know you're going to fail." The meeting has destroyed your confidence. Knowing your future failure makes every challenge feel pointless. Why try if you already know you'll break on Floor 7? The predetermined failure knowledge creates a self-fulfilling prophecy. Your motivation crumbles.
failure.statusEffect: Knowledge of Future Failure - Destroyed Motivation

success.narration: You confront them: "You're not real. You're a test. The game is trying to mess with my head." Your alternate self smiles. "Smart. You're right. I'm a projection designed to influence your choices." Their admission is surprisingly respectful. "But the fact that you figured it out means you're thinking clearly. That's good. You'll need that clarity on Floor 6." The projection dissipates, but not before handing you a special item. "For seeing through the illusion." You passed a test by not accepting the projection as real. Your critical thinking was rewarded. The ability to question reality even when faced with impossible things is crucial for the higher floors. You've proven you have that ability.

failure.narration: You challenge them: "You're not real!" But they respond with information only you would know - memories, secrets, thoughts you've never spoken aloud. "I'm you. I know everything you know because I AM you." The proof is undeniable. But your challenge has offended them. "Fine. If you don't believe me, figure it out yourself." Your alternate self becomes hostile. "I was trying to help but you rejected that. Good luck - you'll need it." They leave, but not before giving you a parting gift - they deliberately cause problems for you. Somehow your alternate self has the power to influence your timeline. Items disappear from your inventory. Nannies become stricter with you specifically. Challenges become harder. Your alternate self is sabotaging you for rejecting their help. The hostile alternate self becomes a recurring antagonist throughout your journey, making everything harder. Your challenge to their existence turned a potential ally into an enemy.
